pets.title: A new lad again at sixty-eight, with everything to prove
pets.description: To the old hands at the gate, by work they can see, and to a body that felt ninety after two hours

pets.title: Watched at the gate, and showing the old hands by work
pets.description: Silence at the gate, a place earned and never asked for, and a modest hope to be one of them

pets.title: Frightened to find out what his body has left
pets.description: Felt ninety after two hours, and a year in a chair that took something from him

pets.title: Surplus since retiring: torn between being needed and left be
pets.description: Shut in, in Pat's way and needed by nothing, and glad of a plot that asks nothing of him

pets.title: “The part left over”, wanting a job that needs him
pets.description: Days indoors, nothing that needs him, Pat relieved, and a life to make from nothing

pets.title: Glad of a plot that waits and does not mind
pets.description: A quiet on the bucket, and wanting the job and nobody wanting him

pets.title: From at a loss before the brambles to proud of a cleared square
pets.description: Not knowing where to start, then a square three yards by three looked at like a rebuilt bus

T1:3:0.text: Nervous at the gate: a new lad again at sixty-eight
quotes: "And they all stopped talking. … I felt like the new lad on his first day at the depot."
notes: Stopped talking: silence as the first greeting. Back to sixteen in a moment. 'Last the week' is the test he expects to sit.

T1:5:0.text: Belonging earned by work, never by talk
quotes: "Nobody talked to you, not properly, till you'd shown you could do a job. … You let the work do the talking."
notes: Belonging earned, never given, and never said: 'You just know.' The depot's rule brought to the plot whole?

T1:7:0.text: Wanting somewhere outdoors after days without sky
quotes: "I'd gone three days without seeing the sky properly. … So I wanted somewhere to be that wasn't indoors. Somewhere with a job waiting for me."
notes: Three days without the sky, counted. Indoors is the loss he names first, before Pat.

T1:9:0.text: Surplus at home since retiring, everything working without him
quotes: "I'm in the way of the hoover. … Everything works without it. That's what retiring's been. I'm the part left over."
notes: Following his wife round the flat. The engine is his trade's image. Not unwanted, surplus: 'everything works without it'.

T1:11:0.text: The plot taken on to be needed again
quotes: "You wake up and there's nothing that needs you. Nobody's going to ring if you don't turn up. … That's a job. That'll need me."
notes: Rung at two in the morning was being needed. Knows the buses by their sound from the ninth floor.

T1:13:0.text: At a loss before two years of brambles
quotes: "I stood there with a brand new fork on Saturday and I didn't know where to start. I just stood. I'm not used to that, not knowing where to start."

T1:15:0.text: Pride at stake: showing the old hands he will last
quotes: "I'm not going to be one that gives up by June. So I want them to see it, the old boys, every time they come through the gate. … You don't tell them. You let them see."
notes: 'Like it was the weather.' Half gone by June heard as a dare. Show, never tell.

T1:17:0.text: Not yet entitled to ask the old hands
quotes: "I'd like to know what they know. But you don't ask. Not yet. You've not earned asking."
notes: Pat's 'only men with sheds' against his 'not how I was brought up'. Is it the old hands or the depot keeping him from asking?

T1:19:0.text: Frightened by a body that felt ninety after two hours digging
quotes: "I felt about ninety. … I thought, what if I can't do it. What if that's me now."
notes: Pat helping him out of the chair. 'A man who can't dig a bit of garden': smaller in his own eyes.

T1:21:0.text: Digging to find out what his body has left
quotes: "Now it's started sending in its own bills. … I suppose that's what it is. I'm finding out what I've got left."
notes: The body that once did as it was told now 'sending in its own bills'. Pacing taken from the trade.

T1:23:0.text: A year in a chair took something from him
quotes: "I've had a year in a chair, and I think it's taken something off me that I didn't know it was taking."
notes: His dad dug past eighty. The doctor's waiting room as a place to be ashamed in.

T1:25:0.text: Nothing asked of him at the plot
quotes: "Nobody needs anything from me down there. At home I'm always about to be asked to move. … I've not done that in years, just sat. I didn't know I could."
notes: The robin. Sitting is new to him: 'I didn't know I could.'

T1:27:0.text: Torn between a job and nobody wanting him
quotes: "I want the job, and I want nobody wanting me. That doesn't make much sense, does it. … It doesn't mind if I sit on a bucket."
notes: Needed and not wanted, both. Notices the contradiction himself. No foreman, no phone, no Pat with the hoover.

T1:29:0.text: A little hurt that Pat is glad to see him go
quotes: "I think she's relieved, if I'm honest, and I don't blame her. … I'd not have minded her being a bit sorry, mind. Just a bit."
notes: 'She meant it nice', said twice. Allows himself a small hurt, then takes it back.

T1:31:0.text: Unwarned that retiring means making a life from nothing
quotes: "At sixty-eight I've got to make myself a life, and I've never had to before, because the depot was my life and it came ready made. … Nobody tells you that, when you retire."
notes: Retiring as starting again 'like a lad'. The new lad at the gate again?

T1:33:0.text: A modest hope: the old hands talking on as he comes in
quotes: "I'd like to walk through that gate one morning and have them carry on talking. Not stop. Just carry on, like I've always been there. That's all. I'd settle for that."
notes: His dad's potatoes. 'I'd settle for that': the hope kept small, the wish not small at all.

T1:35:0.text: Proud of a cleared square like a rebuilt bus
quotes: "Just looked at my square. You'd laugh. Three yards by three, and I stood there looking at it like it was a bus I'd rebuilt."

pets.title: “Here he is”: near enough one of them by midsummer
pets.description: Corrected by Frank and so noticed, taught by Maureen without asking, and greeted at the gate

pets.title: Living at the plot for now, with Pat left missing him
pets.description: A day with a shape at a place that knows him, winter kept from mind, and Pat missing him at home

pets.title: A day with a shape at a place that knows him, till November
pets.description: Waking to the plot, known by the place, minding what he misses, and November pushed away

pets.title: Pat missing him, and the plot brought home to her
pets.description: Missed after all, sweet peas to make it up, and the first potatoes in his cap

pets.title: No longer ashamed, of dead beans or of sitting down
pets.description: A failure laughed off with Maureen, and a body serviced like an engine, its limits known

T2:3:0.text: The plot now the centre of his days, the empty morning gone
quotes: "The flat's where I sleep now, and the plot's where I live. That's how it feels. I wake up and the first thing I think is, I wonder if the onions are all right. Not, what am I going to do with myself."
notes: A door and a chair in the shed: settling a place. The morning's first thought is the onions, not the empty day.

T2:5:0.text: Trying to make it up to Pat for never being there now
quotes: "she said, I didn't marry you for your runner beans. … So I've been trying. I bring her things back. Sweet peas."
notes: 'You can't win with you' taken on the chin. Sweet peas where she can see them from her chair: an apology without words.

T2:7:0.text: Struck to learn Pat missed him
quotes: "I never thought she might miss me. … She said, I got used to you, and now you've gone again. Like the depot all over. And that went in, that did."
notes: He had never thought she might miss him. 'Like the depot all over': he has gone out to work again.

T2:9:0.text: From insult to hello: an old hand correcting him
quotes: "I took it as an insult for a whole day. … it was the first thing he'd said to me that wasn't good morning. … That's how they say hello down there."

T2:13:0.text: Two words from an old hand worth more than a long service plaque
quotes: "Two months of good morning, and then that's better. … that's better from Frank did more for me than the plaque. The plaque's in the cupboard with the Christmas lights."
notes: The plaque in with the Christmas lights. Two words from Frank weigh more than forty-one years' award?

quotes: "And I was embarrassed. Properly embarrassed. I put a bit of netting over them so nobody would see."
notes: Netting like a sheet over a body. Hiding a failure, the depot's habit.

T2:17:0.text: Shame gone once the failure was shared: the year, not him
quotes: "But you can't fix a bean. … And when Maureen laughed, it went out of me, the embarrassment. … It wasn't me. It was the year."
notes: 'It wasn't me. It was the year.' The shame let out 'like the air out of a tyre'.

T2:19:0.text: Taught everything by Maureen without asking, thrown at first
quotes: "I didn't know what to do with it, to be honest. … Everything I know, near enough, Maureen told me. I never asked her one thing. She just told me."
notes: Maureen breaks his rule about asking without him having to. Is that why he can take it from her?

T2:21:0.text: Joy at the first potatoes, carried home to Pat
quotes: "I stood there with them in my hand like I'd found money in the street. My own potatoes. … I took them home in my cap. … She said they were very nice. Very nice. I'll take very nice."
notes: Brambles in March, potatoes in July. Pat's 'very nice' enough for him.

T2:23:0.text: Unafraid of a body whose limits he knows
quotes: "In March I was frightened of it, the body, I told you that. I'm not frightened of it now. I know what it'll do. I know where it stops."

T2:25:0.text: Resting now as servicing an engine
quotes: "In March I was ashamed of that. Sitting down. I felt like I was skiving … Now I think of it as part of the job. … Well I'm the engine."
notes: Rest as servicing, not skiving: a new rule from the old trade.

T2:27:0.text: Days with a shape again, after a year of lumps
quotes: "It's got a shape. That's the thing. … Last year a day was just a lump. … Now I look at the clock and think, is it three already."
notes: A day in two halves with dinner between, 'like a shift'. Time back in his hands.

T2:29:0.text: Known by the place now, no longer a visitor
quotes: "It's like the place knows I'm there. That sounds soft. But it's like that. I'm not a visitor there now."
notes: The robin has a mate now. 'That sounds soft' said before he lets himself say it.

T2:33:0.text: Minding what he misses: part of something again
quotes: "Retiring, you don't miss anything. There's nothing to miss. … I was put out I'd missed a fox. That's how I knew."

T2:37:0.text: Winter dread felt in the chest and pushed down
quotes: "Same feeling as March. Before March. The part left over. It comes up in my chest a bit, and I push it back down. I tell myself it's July."

T2:39:0.text: Greeted at the gate: near enough what he hoped for
quotes: "When I come in now, Frank looks up and says, here he is. … But it's near enough. It's near enough for me. I'll take here he is."
notes: Measures it against March himself. 'Near enough' is his whole stance.

pets.title: Laid low, then carried by the old hands as one of them
pets.description: A fortnight sure he had not lasted, then let in without a word, and worth found in more than what he can do

pets.title: Laid up, and sure he had not lasted
pets.description: Felled in the shed, the part left over again, and the gate's verdict feared

pets.title: Let in without a word, from his potatoes to the rake
pets.description: His potatoes lifted and labelled while he was laid up, help heard as belonging, the rake at the bonfire, Frank's grief seen, and Wednesdays in Frank's shed

pets.title: Worth no longer only in what he can do
pets.description: Nothing looked for wrong in their work, half sacks without shame, and the back sure to go again

pets.title: Hearing himself go quiet at the gate: an old hand now
pets.description: Uneasy and a bit pleased at the newcomer, handing on Frank's ways, and glad to be asked

pets.title: Seen and heard at home at last, through the plot
pets.description: News of his own for Pat, Pat seeing his work, and neighbours met over potatoes

pets.title: Surplus no more, except in the winter flat
pets.description: Not surplus at the plot, and winter feared as a Sunday night at the bus station

T3:3:0.text: Helpless as a beetle when his back went
quotes: "something went at the bottom of my back, like a cable snapping. Down I went. … I couldn't get up. … there's me on the floor like a beetle."
notes: Starts with 'the bad bit, because it's the bit that matters'. Like a beetle: laughs at himself even on the floor.

T3:5:0.text: Laid up: worse for knowing what he was missing
quotes: "it was the part left over again, only worse, because now I knew what I was missing."
"They'll be saying it at the gate. Told you. Another one who didn't last. Sixty-eight, and his back went, and that was him."
notes: Worse than last winter because now he knows what he is missing. The gate's verdict heard in advance.

T3:5:1.text: Sure the old hands would say he had not lasted
quotes: "it was the part left over again, only worse, because now I knew what I was missing."
"They'll be saying it at the gate. Told you. Another one who didn't last. Sixty-eight, and his back went, and that was him."
notes: Worse than last winter because now he knows what he is missing. The gate's verdict heard in advance.

T3:7:0.text: Overcome to find his potatoes lifted and labelled by others
quotes: "Somebody had dug my plot. … Nobody'd said a word. I stood in my shed and I'll be honest with you, I had to sit down, and it wasn't my back."
notes: Paper sacks, labels in marker pen. 'It wasn't my back': moved, and says it only sideways.

quotes: "a year ago, if somebody had dug my plot, that's what I'd have heard. I'd have been ashamed. … And this time it was the other way round. … You don't dig for somebody who's not one of you."
notes: The same act, help, heard the other way round. What changed: the plot, or him?

T3:11:0.text: A man no longer only what he can do
quotes: "A man's what he can do. So you lie on a settee a fortnight and you can't do anything, and what are you then. … And I didn't look for anything wrong with it. I didn't want to."
notes: 'What was I for.' Worth as doing, held for forty-one years, let go in a shed.

T3:15:0.text: On the rake: no longer new or watched
quotes: "That I'm one of the furniture now. … You're not new any more. You're not being watched. You're on the rake. … Best night I've had in years."
notes: Better than his leaving do, which had a buffet. One of the furniture, the word he could not use in March.

T3:17:0.text: Trusted with an old hand's grief
quotes: "But Frank told a story. About his wife … And Ken put his hand on his shoulder, just for a second. … I'm being let see this, because I'm one of them."
notes: Let see Frank's grief. Being trusted with it is what belonging means here.

T3:19:0.text: Not proud to hear himself go quiet at a newcomer, as they did to him
quotes: "we all stopped talking. All three of us. Me with them. And I heard us do it. I heard myself go quiet, the same as they did to me."
notes: Purple hair, a little dog. He hears the silence from inside it now.

T3:21:0.text: Uneasy and a bit pleased to be an insider
quotes: "I didn't like it. And I did, a bit. Both. … it meant I was on the right side of the gate now. That's the truth."
"And I told her her bed was too close to the hedge. Which is exactly what Frank did to me. … It goes round, doesn't it. It goes round."
notes: 'The right side of the gate', and he knows there is a wrong one. Frank's onions become his hedge.

T3:21:1.text: Hearing himself pass on what Frank did to him
quotes: "I didn't like it. And I did, a bit. Both. … it meant I was on the right side of the gate now. That's the truth."
"And I told her her bed was too close to the hedge. Which is exactly what Frank did to me. … It goes round, doesn't it. It goes round."
notes: 'The right side of the gate', and he knows there is a wrong one. Frank's onions become his hedge.

T3:23:0.text: Glad to be asked, his March rule on asking gone
quotes: "And I told her, and I didn't think less of her for asking. That's changed and all. In March I said you don't ask, you've not earned asking."
notes: The March rule on asking undone in his own words. Wishes he had asked Frank.

T3:25:0.text: Neighbours of eleven years met at last over a bag of potatoes
quotes: "people I'd never spoken to in eleven years in that block knocked on my door to say thank you. … Eleven years, and it took a bag of potatoes."
notes: A cake in the bag. Home as well as the plot opening out.

T3:27:0.text: Home from the plot with news of his own for Pat
quotes: "She says I come back from the plot with things to say. … I didn't have things to say before. … A man needs a bit of news of his own, I think."
notes: No news since retiring. 'Something that's happened to him': a life with events in it again.

T3:31:0.text: Seen by Pat in his own work at last
quotes: "Forty-one years she never saw what I did. And this time she came and sat in it. … I don't think I knew I wanted it till she was sat there."
notes: Forty-one years of work Pat never saw. The want found only when it was met.

T3:35:0.text: Winter feared as a Sunday night at the bus station
quotes: "Like the bus station on a Sunday night. All the buses in, all lined up, lights off, nothing going anywhere. That's what I'm frightened of."
"He said, you'll come Wednesdays. He didn't ask. He said. So maybe there's that. Maybe it won't be a Sunday night."
notes: A Sunday night at the bus station: his own trade's image for empty time. Frank tells, does not ask.

T3:35:1.text: A winter hope: told to come Wednesdays
quotes: "Like the bus station on a Sunday night. All the buses in, all lined up, lights off, nothing going anywhere. That's what I'm frightened of."
"He said, you'll come Wednesdays. He didn't ask. He said. So maybe there's that. Maybe it won't be a Sunday night."
notes: A Sunday night at the bus station: his own trade's image for empty time. Frank tells, does not ask.

T3:37:0.text: Half sacks no longer shameful, two trips more time there
quotes: "In March I'd have been ashamed of half sacks. Now I think, well, there's two trips instead of one. Two trips is more time down there. I've got the time."

T3:39:0.text: Sure someone would lift his potatoes next time
quotes: "It'll go again. I'm sixty-eight, it'll go again, I know that now. … But I know now that if it does, somebody'd lift my spuds."
"And I'm not the part left over. Not down there. Up in the flat, some days, still, I won't lie. But not down there."
notes: Ends where March began, on the part left over, and turns it.

T3:39:1.text: Not surplus at the plot, if still in the flat
quotes: "It'll go again. I'm sixty-eight, it'll go again, I know that now. … But I know now that if it does, somebody'd lift my spuds."
"And I'm not the part left over. Not down there. Up in the flat, some days, still, I won't lie. But not down there."
notes: Ends where March began, on the part left over, and turns it.
